Track backlog age, recovery success, escalation rate and worker freshness; detect loss of the monitoring process itself.

Exchange operators receive critical alerts through an operator dashboard and email. Alert delivery is independent of the monitored recovery worker, allowing alerts when that worker stops. When operator email delivery fails, Exchange retains the alert, retries delivery with increasing delays and shows the delivery failure on the operator dashboard. Failed delivery never counts as acknowledgement or stops recovery. Exchange keeps one pending operator email per incident and recipient, updating it with the latest status instead of accumulating every reminder. If the incident is acknowledged or resolved before sending, Exchange suppresses the pending alert and preserves its history. For temporary operator email delivery failures, Exchange waits 1, 2, 5, then 15 minutes between attempts, capped at 15 minutes thereafter, while the incident remains unresolved and unacknowledged. Reminders update the same pending email. Permanent operator email failures pause delivery to the affected address, retain the alert and show “Operator action required” on the operator dashboard. An authorized operator must correct the configuration and explicitly resume delivery. Other recipients remain unaffected. MVP critical operator alerts use an operator-managed list of verified email addresses. Each listed recipient receives critical alerts, subject to existing delivery-pause rules.
